songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: Tight ’66 set with blistering Dancing In The Street jam and strong blues.
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a high‑energy blues‑rock workout highlighted by a scorching Dancing In The Street jam and a powerful Midnight Hour finish. Jerry’s lead work is front‑and‑center while Pigpen’s organ drives the early numbers. Recording quality is solid for 1966, making this a must‑listen snapshot of the Dead’s formative sound.
ai_show_review.review: On September 16 1966 at San Francisco’s Avalon Ballroom the Grateful Dead captured a youthful, high‑octane set that still feels fresh today. The band rides a tight blues groove from the opening “I Know You Rider” through Pigpen‑driven numbers like “It Hurts Me Too,” “Good Morning Little School Girl,” and “Lindy.” The centerpiece is an exuberant “Dancin' In The Street” jam where Jerry’s scorching, jazz‑inflected solo rockets over swirling organ, earning repeated praise as “hot” and “smoking” in the mix. The encore “In The Midnight Hour” closes the night with a soulful punch, showcasing the group’s tight rhythm section. Across all six recordings – three soundboard sources and two audience captures – listeners report clear, balanced audio that holds up remarkably well for a 1966 tape, making this set one of the clearest windows into the early Dead’s raw power.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with good balance, minimal tape noise and the most complete representation of the tight performance.

key_highlights: Scorching “Dancin' In The Street” jam with Jerry’s front‑and‑center solo work.
Powerful closing “In The Midnight Hour” that caps the high‑energy blues set.
Strong vocal and rhythmic delivery on “Good Morning Little School Girl” and “It Hurts Me Too”.
Soundboard recordings provide unusually clear audio for a 1966 show.
song_highlights: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers blistering, jazz‑inflected solos—especially on “Dancin' In The Street” and “It Hurts Me Too”—and is front‑and‑center in the mix throughout.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a steady bass foundation that underpins the high‑energy blues rocking of the set.
band_performance.Bob: Vocals are notably stronger than typical ’66 recordings, and his rhythm guitar work adds solid support to the band’s drive.
band_performance.Billy: Drums lock in with Jerry in a tight “question‑and‑answer” dynamic that lifts the entire performance.

must_listen_sequences: It's All Over Now Baby Blue
